statement: Sweeps a saved 2D profile along an edge path to create a smart 3D object (walls, moldings, framing) whose profile and path remain editable.

source.ref: Profile Builder: sweep saved profile along path

superiority: Native, procedural, undoable path sweep with mitre, twist and scale-along-path controls, no extension install needed.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Sweep a rectangular profile along an L-shaped path; volume equals profile area times path length (with mitred corners) within 1e-6 relative; edit the profile and the object updates.

statement: Sets profile height, width, rotation and offset relative to the path with control of orientation at corners.

source.ref: Profile Builder: profile size, orientation and offset along the path

superiority: Same controls as live parameters with numeric fields.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Set width 90 mm, rotation 15 degrees, offset 10 mm; section positions equal closed form within 1e-6.

statement: Smart-Path selects connected edge chains and parametric assemblies combine several profiles and components along one path.

source.ref: Profile Builder: Smart-Path select and assemblies

superiority: Assemblies are editable layered compositions with materials and quantities.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Build a 3-profile wall assembly along a path; each layer's volume equals its profile area times length.

statement: Creates parametric holes and openings in profile-built objects such as windows and doors in walls.
superiority: Openings keep a live relation to the door or window object.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Cut a 900 x 2100 opening; the remaining wall volume equals total minus opening volume within 1e-6.

statement: Libraries of reusable profiles and a quantifier that reports lengths and quantities of built objects.

source.ref: Profile Builder: profile libraries and Quantifier (lengths and quantities)

superiority: Quantities are model-native schedules with live updates.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Quantifier lengths of 10 built members equal path lengths within 1 mm.

statement: Merges coplanar adjacent faces and removes the shared edges while keeping materials.
superiority: Merge honors materials and attributes and shows a preview of what will change.
notes: Acceptance sketch: A triangulated planar quad mesh merges into the original polygons; area preserved to 1e-9 relative.

statement: Erases hidden geometry, stray edges not bounding a face and duplicate edges and faces.

source.ref: CleanUp: erase hidden, stray and duplicate geometry

superiority: Reports each removed entity and can be undone as one step.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Fixture with 20 stray edges: all removed, solid faces untouched.

statement: Repairs split or overlapping edges, purges unused materials, removes lines not connected to anything.

source.ref: CleanUp: repair edges, erase unused materials and unconnected geometry

superiority: Idempotent: a second run changes nothing.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Overlapping edges fixture is repaired to a clean edge graph.

statement: Cleanup has a merge tolerance, can run on a selection or the model, and exposes a command to repeat the last settings.

source.ref: CleanUp: tolerance settings, selection scope and scripting

superiority: Deterministic, scriptable and parallelized for million-face models.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Run twice with the same settings; second run reports zero changes.

statement: Highlights geometry that prevents a group from being a solid: surface borders, extra edges, internal faces, reversed faces, overlapping faces, small edges.

source.ref: Solid Inspector: detect shell errors (holes, extra edges, internal faces, reversed faces, face overlap, short edges)

superiority: Built into the application with fix-all and a heat-map of defects.
notes: Acceptance sketch: A cube with one face removed reports one border loop; with an internal face reports it.

statement: Offers to fix many reported errors and steps through errors with a zoom.

source.ref: Solid Inspector: automatic fix and navigation between errors

superiority: Fixes preserve materials and attributes with a before/after diff.
notes: Acceptance sketch: After fix-all on a fixture with 5 repairable defects the group passes the solid check.

statement: Creates a surface by lofting through selected contours (open or closed) with twist and matching options.
superiority: NURBS loft with exact surfaces and continuity control.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Loft between circle r=1 at z=0 and circle r=2 at z=3; the lateral area equals the cone-frustum formula within tessellation error.

statement: Sweeps contours along a path to build a surface.
superiority: Same with rail-guided orientation and exact surface.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Square contour along a quarter circle; surface bounding box equals closed form within 1e-6.

statement: Builds a surface through contours guided by rail curves.
superiority: Network-surface kernel with tolerances.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Two rails and two contours; edges of the result lie on the rails within 1e-6.

statement: Includes spline creation and options for skinning (closed, spline fit, face generation).

source.ref: Curviloft: spline, polygon and skin options

superiority: Native curves.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Fit a spline through 8 points; passes through them within 1e-9.

statement: Shared library required by the Fredo6 extension family (UI, localization, geometry helpers, licensing).
superiority: No shared third-party library is needed because the capabilities are built in.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Install order and dependency check: extension refuses to run without the library.

statement: Extrudes faces with correct side joints for thick shells of curved or multi-face surfaces.

source.ref: Joint Push Pull: joint push pull on faces

superiority: Shell thickness is exact and keeps a live parameter.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Thicken a hemispherical surface by 5 mm; resulting solid volume equals shell volume within tessellation error.

statement: Variants such as Vector Push Pull, Normal Push Pull and incremental/to-target-plane Push Pull.

source.ref: Joint Push Pull: vector, normal and incremental modes

superiority: Same modes as options of the native push/pull.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Vector push along (1,0,1) of a face; side faces parallel to the vector.

statement: Round Push Pull creates a rounded transition while extruding.

source.ref: Joint Push Pull: round push pull and chamfer variants

superiority: Exact fillet surface.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Round push of a box face with radius r; fillet cross-section equals circular arc.

statement: Deformation tools: non-uniform scale, taper, twist, bend and stretch of selected geometry with interactive handles.

source.ref: FredoScale: scale, bend, twist, taper, stretch

superiority: Deformations are non-destructive modifiers with parameters.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Twist a box by 90 degrees about z; a vertex at height h rotates by 90*h/H within 1e-9.

statement: Rounds or chamfers edges and vertices on faces and solids.

source.ref: Round Corner (FredoCorner): round corners and chamfers

superiority: Variable-radius and G2 fillets on exact surfaces.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Fillet an edge of a cube with r=2 mm; cross-section is a quarter circle within tolerance.

statement: Draw Bezier, cubic and spline curves with handles and edit them.
superiority: Native curves with continuity constraints.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Evaluate Bezier at 20 parameters; points equal Bernstein formula within 1e-12.

statement: Draws lines, arcs, circles, Bezier and offsets directly on curved surfaces.
superiority: Surface-aware drawing on exact surfaces.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Draw a circle on a sphere; points lie on the sphere within 1e-6 and equal geodesic radius.

statement: Paints materials through geometry and across connected faces with variants.
superiority: Material layers.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Paint through two layers; target faces receive the material.

statement: Cloth simulation to drape fabric over objects.
superiority: Native physics.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Drape a plane on a sphere; no interpenetration within tolerance.

statement: Family of extrusion tools for edges and faces.

source.ref: ExtrudeTools (extrude edges by rails, vector, normal, lathe)

superiority: Native sweep and loft with history.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Extrude edge along a rail; result face count and area equal closed form.

statement: Subdivides a mesh with smooth subdivision (Catmull-Clark style) and smooths.
superiority: True SubD with creases and a GPU limit surface.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Subdivide a cube once; result has 24 faces and limit-surface point matches Catmull-Clark formula.

statement: Works on a selection and sets creases to keep sharp edges.

source.ref: Artisan: Subdivide Selection, Smooth Selection and Crease Tool

superiority: Edge weight control on a SubD kernel.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Crease one edge; the edge remains sharp, adjacent faces smooth.

statement: Brush tools on mesh vertices with soft selection and radius.

source.ref: Artisan: sculpt, smooth, inflate, flatten and pinch

superiority: Sculpting with dyntopo and layers.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Inflate brush on a plane; displacement follows the falloff curve.

statement: Move, rotate and scale vertices with soft selection falloff.

source.ref: Artisan: vertex transform with soft selection

superiority: Proportional editing on any mesh.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Soft move of a vertex; neighbors follow the selected falloff.

statement: Flattens selected faces to a plane and reduces polygon count.

source.ref: Artisan: make planar and polygon reduction

superiority: Quadric decimation with feature preservation.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Reduce a mesh to 50 percent triangles; deviation below tolerance.

statement: Quad-based subdivision modeling extension with edge loops and creases.
superiority: Native SubD.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Subdivision level 2 vertex count matches formula.

statement: Scatters instances (grass, trees, rocks) on surfaces, along curves or at points with density, random rotation and scale.

source.ref: Skatter: scatter on surfaces, curves and points

superiority: Procedural scatter with seeds and masks that stays editable and renders as instances.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Scatter 1000 instances on a 10x10 m surface at density 10 per m2; count within 5 percent and all instances lie on the surface.

statement: Interactive brushes add and remove instances; exclusion zones avoid obstacles.

source.ref: Skatter: paint-in and erase brushes, masks and exclusion zones

superiority: Same plus mask maps.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Brush a region; no instance falls inside an exclusion zone.

statement: Instances are exported efficiently to supported renderers.
superiority: Native GPU instancing.
notes: Acceptance sketch: 100k instances render with memory below limit.

statement: Fills a roof or ground surface with PV panels with orientation, tilt and spacing options and panel database.
superiority: Panel layout with shading and yield analysis built in.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Fill a 10x6 m roof with 1.7x1.0 m panels, 0.02 m gaps: panel count equals closed-form packing count.

statement: Shading range analysis, sun path diagrams and energy reports (Pro).

source.ref: Skelion: shadow analysis, sun path and energy report

superiority: Integrated with the Analysis Hub.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Shading hours on a fixture match solar position reference.

statement: Solid operations that modify containers in place and fit the workflow of the native tools.
superiority: Native booleans with in-place option.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Union and subtract produce volumes equal to closed forms; originals edited in place.

statement: Extrudes a face along the vertical direction in a way that keeps verticality for slanted faces.
superiority: Direction option on native push/pull.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Extrude a slanted face upright; side walls vertical within 1e-9.

statement: Rotates an object to align with a plane selected in the model.
superiority: Align-to-face as a native Rotate mode.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Rotate to plane; object normal equals plane normal within 1e-9.

statement: Selection helpers such as grow selection, shrink, select by loops and faces.
superiority: Native selection algebra.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Grow selection by one ring; selected set equals neighbors.

statement: Edit mesh vertices and edges directly with transform tools and soft selection.
superiority: Native mesh edit mode.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Vertex move updates adjacent faces correctly.

statement: Draw, edit and connect quad faces and loops with edge-loop selection.
superiority: Native edge loops and ring selection.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Select an edge loop on a quad grid; count equals loop size.

statement: UV mapping and unwrapping tools for texturing models.
superiority: Native UV editor.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Unwrap a cube; UV islands do not overlap and total area matches.

statement: Creates Bezier patch surfaces with control grids.
superiority: Exact NURBS patches.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Evaluate patch at 25 (u,v) points; equals Bernstein formula within 1e-12.

statement: Collection of edge selection and manipulation tools.
superiority: Native filters.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Select edges by length range; counts equal.

statement: Real-time section views with hatch fills and 2D section output for drawings.

source.ref: Skalp: section fill and live section views

superiority: Native section fill with hatches and drawing output.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Live section equals native section within tolerance and fill follows material hatches.

statement: Parametric wall framing with studs, plates, headers and openings.
superiority: Parametric walls with data and schedules.
notes: Acceptance sketch: 4 m wall at 400 mm stud spacing: stud count equals formula; opening headers present.

statement: Parametric roof truss generation with member sizes and connections.
superiority: Parametric trusses with structural data.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Pitch 4:12, span 8 m: heel height and member lengths equal closed form.

statement: Parametric foundation and footing generation.
superiority: Parametric foundations with quantities.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Footing dimensions match inputs.

statement: Draws plans in 2D style and converts to 3D walls, openings and floors.
superiority: Native wall objects.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Wall of thickness 200 mm and height 3 m; volume equals length x 0.2 x 3.

statement: Creates inflated, minimal surface shapes from boundaries.
superiority: Physical surface relaxation.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Minimal surface bounded by a loop; mean curvature near zero.

statement: Physics simulation of rigid bodies with joints inside SketchUp.
superiority: Native physics with recorded animation.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Drop a box; free-fall position equals 0.5 g t^2 within 1 percent.

statement: Opens and shares models with Trimble Connect from within SketchUp.
superiority: Local-first sync with branching and merge rather than file-level sharing.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Share a model and reload it in a second session; content hash equals and permissions apply.

statement: Classify and manage IFC data in models.
superiority: IFC 4.3 classification with IDS checks and issue reports.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Classify 20 elements and export IFC; class counts and property sets equal the source classification.

statement: Real-time rendering and walkthrough synced live with the model.
superiority: Real-time path-traced renderer built into the viewport, so no live-link process or second geometry copy is needed.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Edit a material and move the camera; the live viewport reflects both within 1 s and matches a reference render within SSIM 0.97.

statement: Live link to Twinmotion for real-time visualization.
superiority: Built-in real-time visualization with animation and asset scattering, no exchange step.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Move an object in the modeling view; the linked scene updates within 1 s and material assignments transfer.

statement: Live synchronization with Lumion.
superiority: Built-in real-time renderer with the same environment and entourage tools.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Change geometry and a material; the synced scene updates within 1 s with correct instance transforms.

statement: Photoreal path-traced rendering extension.
superiority: Native path tracer.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Render a Cornell-box scene; RMS error vs reference below threshold at N samples.

statement: Unbiased and biased rendering with material library.
superiority: Built-in unbiased path tracer with the same material model and denoiser.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Render a calibrated reference scene; mean luminance within 2 percent of the reference value at equal sample count.

statement: Rendering extension with a content browser.
superiority: Built-in renderer plus an open asset browser with provenance.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Render a reference interior; image statistics within tolerance of the reference and entourage inserted at correct scale.

statement: Physically based renderer integration.
superiority: Built-in physically based path tracer with spectral option.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Render a Cornell-box scene; RMS error against a converged reference below threshold at fixed samples.

statement: In-app library of 3D assets for rendering.
superiority: Open asset library with licence and provenance metadata on each asset.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Insert a library asset; units, scale, origin and materials are correct and instances are shared.

statement: Imports Gaussian splats as reality context.
superiority: Native splat rendering with section and depth integration against model geometry.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Load a sample splat; splat count equals the file header and visibility and clipping toggles work.

statement: Streams models to Vision Pro.
superiority: Streaming with LOD to any XR headset over open standards (OpenXR).
notes: Acceptance sketch: Stream a 200k-triangle model; frame latency under the device target and 1:1 scale within 1 percent.

statement: Utility set for welding edges and TIG family utilities.
superiority: Native weld with tolerance and preview.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Weld five connected edges; one curve entity with five segments results.
